meta.title: Autorestart — restart continuation
meta.description: Keeps agent work alive across a DeepSeek Harness restart: a durable checkpoint, goal re-arm or a continuation message on boot, and an idle-aware graceful restart the agent can request itself.

backupChoice.title: Automatic pre-restart backup: include the installed plugins too?
backupChoice.body: A snapshot of the current configuration is taken before every restart, so a host that fails to come back can be rolled back automatically.
backupChoice.withPluginsHint: About 3 seconds and 117 MB more; a plugin that breaks the boot can be rolled back too.
backupChoice.configOnlyHint: Instant, about 66 KB; plugin problems cannot be rolled back and need a manual reinstall.
backupChoice.footnote: You can change this later in Settings → Auto-restart & shut down

seconds.label: Shutdown countdown seconds
seconds.hint: Once every conversation is done, this countdown is shown on screen (pick "Never mind, keep it on" to cancel); the machine goes off when it reaches zero. Raise it when you want more time to write.

restartGrace.label: Wait before the restart
restartGrace.hint: A restart has no countdown: the host restarts as soon as the conversations are done. Raise this if you rely on a memory or summary plugin that writes its notes after the conversation ended (default 0 seconds).

backup.label: Backup before a restart
backup.hint: Take a snapshot of the current configuration before every restart, so a host that cannot boot again is rolled back automatically.

backupPlugins.label: Include the installed plugins in the backup
backupPlugins.hint: Off: only the state of DSH itself is backed up — the plugin directory of the profile is left out.

supervisor.capableYes: available: the host comes back on its own
supervisor.capableNo: not available: the host does not come back on its own
supervisor.startup.container: in a container (the orchestrator is in charge)
supervisor.startup.selfSupervised: the supervisor of this plugin is in charge
supervisor.startup.unknown: it could not be established who started it
supervisor.hint: The supervisor is a process of its own: it starts at login, it starts the host again when its process is gone, and it restores the last snapshot when the host does not come up. No administrator rights needed.
supervisor.noInstallDesktop: The desktop app restarts itself — there is no supervisor to install here.
supervisor.noInstallExternal: Another supervisor is already in charge of this host. A second one would start the host as well and both would fight over the port, so there is nothing to install here.
supervisor.noInstallUnknown: The host did not say who starts it, so there is nothing to install here.
supervisor.accessHint: The token changes with every restart, and so does the link. This one is always the current one.
supervisor.pending: The uninstall did not finish. Please run it by hand: {commands}
supervisor.noCommand: No replayable restart command could be derived
supervisor.reason.ok: This command starts this DSH again.
supervisor.reason.desktop-app: The desktop app restarts itself; there is no command to write.
supervisor.reason.not-a-web-host: This DSH is not a web host: it has no port and no listener.
supervisor.reason.argv-unavailable: The command line cannot be read back (it was started in a special way), so nothing is guessed.
supervisor.reason.external-supervisor: Another supervisor is already in charge: a second one would fight over the port. The restart becomes "exit gracefully and let it start me again".
supervisor.reason.container-no-init: This machine has no "at login" (a container), so no automatic start is promised.
supervisor.reason.port-not-fixable: The port changes every time, so the browser would be logged out; the port has to be fixed first.
supervisor.reason.supervised: The supervisor of this plugin is in charge: the restart is handed to it.

supervisor.title: Let DSH bring itself back up?
supervisor.body: This hosted DSH instance is started by hand (or by something else) — when it dies it does not come back. I can install a supervisor of my own: it starts at login, it starts the host again when the process is gone, and it restores the last snapshot when the host does not come up. The supervisor never touches your session data; it only starts, watches and rolls back.
supervisor.changes: What it changes: a new <stateDir>/supervisor/ directory (the supervisor script, its configuration, its log and its lock); on Windows a login record (the scheduled task dsh-autorestart-web), on Linux a systemd user service. What it does NOT change: your session data, your model configuration, the installed plugins.
supervisor.rights: Which rights it needs: on Windows NO administrator rights (it runs "at login"; if the machine forbids ordinary users from creating scheduled tasks, it falls back to the startup folder, which needs none either); on Linux it needs write access to your own home directory (systemctl --user — an ordinary user is enough).
supervisor.uninstall: How to remove it: one click on "Start at login → Uninstall" in the settings; or by hand: schtasks /Delete /TN "dsh-autorestart-web" /F (on Linux: systemctl --user disable --now dsh-autorestart-web.service && rm ~/.config/systemd/user/dsh-autorestart-web.service). Both ways also delete the <stateDir>/supervisor/ directory.
supervisor.installHint: It writes a supervisor script into <stateDir>/supervisor/ and registers a login record on Windows / a systemd user service on Linux. No administrator rights needed. After that the host is started again within seconds when its process is gone; when it does not come up, the snapshot of the last restart is restored. You can uninstall it with one click at any time.
supervisor.keep: Keep the way I start it
supervisor.keepHint: Nothing is changed. Whatever starts the host today keeps starting it. The price: the host does not come back by itself when its process is gone — the restart only works while something else (a docker "restart: always", your own systemd unit) brings it back.
supervisor.laterHint: This card does not come back. You can install the supervisor by hand at any time in "Settings → Auto-restart & shut down → Start at login".

choice.title: Keep the graceful shutdown button?
choice.body: It lives at the very bottom of the left sidebar, next to the Settings button: one click waits for every session to finish, counts down and powers the machine off.
choice.keepHint: One moon button at the bottom of the left sidebar: one click to shut down gracefully.
choice.hideHint: The interface stays as it is; turn it on again in the settings whenever you want it.
choice.footnote: You can change this later in Settings → Auto-restart & shut down
choice.diagramLabel: The button sits at the bottom of the left sidebar, next to Settings

announcement.title: New feature: graceful shutdown
announcement.line1: There is a new 🌙 "Shut down" button at the very bottom of the left sidebar.
announcement.line2: Click it → once every conversation is done it counts down {n} seconds and powers the machine off.
announcement.line2Generic: Click it → once every conversation is done it counts down a few seconds and powers the machine off.
announcement.line3: To change that, go to "Settings → Auto-restart & shut down".
announcement.disabled: The button is currently switched off; you can turn it on in the settings.
